context:
Fix the missing context at the caller boundary first, then remove the
downstream compensation that existed only because the caller failed to pass
that context.

Implement in thin vertical slices:
1. Benchmark identity contract and SQL runner propagation
2. Base adapter routing and validation cleanup
3. Base adapter dialect and single-query cleanup
4. Live result creation and export cleanup
5. Dry-run contract cleanup
6. Doris config ownership cleanup
7. SingleStore config ownership cleanup
8. Regression tests and final audit

Treat compatibility code as an explicit exception boundary. Live execution
paths should become simpler; compatibility import/export paths may retain
fallback behavior where they truly own legacy artifact adaptation.
description:
A targeted architectural review found 5 confirmed non-data-loading instances
of wrong-layer compensation.

Confirmed findings:
1. SQL lifecycle omits canonical benchmark identity even though the caller
   already has it, so the base adapter infers benchmark type from benchmark
   object internals for routing, dialect selection, and row-count validation.
2. Live result creation and export paths re-derive benchmark_id from
   benchmark names instead of receiving a caller-supplied canonical id.
3. Dry-run query extraction and resource estimation ignore
   BenchmarkConfig.name and re-infer benchmark identity from benchmark
   object attributes.
4. Doris resolves host/user/password/database in the config builder, then
   re-resolves env/defaults again in from_config() and __init__().
5. SingleStore has the same duplicated connection/database ownership split.

The fix is not to centralize more inference. The fix is to make the caller
pass the context it already owns, then delete downstream compensation in the
live execution path. Historical artifact compatibility fallbacks and
legitimate owner-layer discovery are explicitly out of scope.

anti_patterns.dont: delete historical result compatibility fallbacks in schema/loader code
anti_patterns.instead: remove only live-path dependence on them

anti_patterns.dont: let config builders and adapters both own env/default resolution for the same connection fields
anti_patterns.why: that guarantees drift and split behavior across callers

anti_patterns.dont: replace multiple sniffers with one centralized infer-benchmark helper
anti_patterns.instead: make callers pass benchmark identity explicitly
anti_patterns.why: that preserves the wrong ownership boundary

anti_patterns.dont: use display names, wrapper class names, or benchmark._name as the authoritative routing input once the caller already has benchmark_config.name

deferrals.reason: The review found similar-looking patterns, but not enough caller-context proof to classify them as confirmed wrong-layer compensation in the current flows

work_units.notes:
Contract documented in benchbox/core/schemas.py docstrings for both
RunConfig and BenchmarkConfig.

Ownership hierarchy (CLI -> persistence):
- BenchmarkConfig.name  -> authoritative slug from CLI/orchestrator (e.g. "tpch")
- RunConfig.benchmark   -> propagated copy; runner must populate from BenchmarkConfig.name
- execution_metadata["benchmark_id"] -> normalised form written to results/export
- display_name / wrapper class names -> presentation only, never routing inputs

Fix sequence: runner populates RunConfig.benchmark (w2), adapter uses
run_config["benchmark"] instead of sniffing (w3/w4), results/export consume
explicit benchmark_id from execution_metadata (w5/w6), dry-run uses
benchmark_config.name directly (w7).

work_units.notes:
643 tests pass across all touched surfaces.

Surviving fallback sites (all confirmed valid):

Benchmark identity in adapter/dryrun:
- _get_benchmark_type() (adapter.py ~1717): the encapsulated fallback method;
  only called when no explicit slug is available from run_config. Live path
  never reaches it: run_config["benchmark_name"] is preferred in all
  _execute_* routing methods.
- "or getattr(benchmark, '_name', ...)" patterns in _get_dialect_queries,
  _execute_all_queries, _execute_single_query, _estimate_resources,
  _estimate_memory_usage: all are documented as fallbacks for callers that
  pre-date explicit slug propagation. Live path from runner always provides
  the slug via run_config["benchmark_name"].

Doris/SingleStore env vars:
- _build_doris_config() and _build_singlestore_config(): single canonical
  resolvers for the CLI path. All env vars are HERE.
- from_config() in both adapters: only DORIS_DATABASE / SINGLESTORE_DATABASE
  env var remains, for benchmark-derived database naming. This is the
  legitimate owner layer (from_config has benchmark+scale_factor context).
- __init__() in both adapters: no env vars, Python defaults only.
work_units.summary: Run focused verification and post-fix audits to ensure only legitimate compatibility boundaries still use fallbacks
